alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction causing viraemia
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. Carbamazepine was started 2 weeks ago, and the viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL in that interval. The temporal relationship strongly supports drug attribution. The patient reports good adherence, further supporting the interaction as the cause. This interaction is directly dose-dependent and clinically significant.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid as per guideline recommendation, or consult neurology for alternative antiepileptic. Repeat viral load after adjustment.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Carbamazepine level is 14 mcg/mL, above the therapeutic range of 4–12. Symptoms include dizziness, ataxia, nystagmus, and tremor, all consistent with toxicity. Hyponatraemia at 128 mmol/L may also be carbamazepine-induced SIADH. The clinician plans dose reduction, which is appropriate. Sodium valproate is already prescribed and is the guideline-recommended alternative for seizure control in patients on DTG.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level, and monitor sodium. Consider switching to valproic acid monotherapy to resolve both toxicity and the DTG interaction.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires adherence support
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for VL >50 copies/mL on DTG-based ART, clinicians should provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects affecting adherence, and repeat VL in 2–3 months. The plan does not mention enhanced adherence counselling or a repeat VL timeline. Addressing the carbamazepine interaction is essential, but adherence support and follow-up VL are still required per protocol.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address side-effects, and repeat viral load in 2–3 months as per guideline.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT with hepatotoxic drugs
alerts.message: ALT is 68 U/L, above normal. The patient is on both sodium valproate and carbamazepine, which are both known hepatotoxic agents. Either drug could be contributing. The recent carbamazepine initiation 2 weeks ago makes it a likely contributor. Non-drug causes such as viral hepatitis should also be considered. No LFT monitoring plan is documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor LFTs regularly while on dual antiepileptics. Investigate viral hepatitis if ALT persists or worsens.
